content.title: About
content.content: Pork with chili and tomatoes is a dish where tender pieces of pork are simmered with hot chili peppers and ripe tomatoes. The combination of meat, the spicy kick of chili, and the sweet‑tart flavor of tomatoes creates a rich, aromatic sauce suitable for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Chili peppers contain capsaicin, which gives the heat and can boost metabolism.
Pork provides high‑quality protein, vitamin B12, and zinc.
The dish is popular in Latin American and Asian cuisines, often enhanced with fresh herbs and spices.
Tomatoes and chili together improve iron absorption from the meat.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork supplies complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from tomatoes and vitamin B12 from pork help maintain a healthy immune system.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene in tomatoes and capsaicin in chili help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Capsaicin stimulates gastric secretions, aiding digestion.

items.title: Heart‑healthy fats
items.content: Lean cuts of pork contain monounsaturated fats that can support healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Adding soy sauce or extra salt can make the dish high in sodium, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Chili heat
items.content: Too much chili may irritate the stomach of people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Pork must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C to eliminate salmonella and trichinella.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato juice.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear pork pieces until golden, then add diced onion, garlic, and chili. Simmer with tomato puree, broth, and spices for 20‑30 minutes until the meat is tender. Serve over rice, quinoa, or garnish with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
